The purpose of this report is to provide background information on the neighborhood land development fund.
This fund is the holding account of Saskatoon lands neighborhood land developments that accumulate the expenditures and revenues related to those developments.

As these neighborhoods get developed and built out, surplus funds are used to help pay for the expenditures for the next neighborhood, as well as provide excess funds that are declared as dividends and transferred to the city's general fund.

There's no formal policy on the allocation regarding the use of these dividends, a guideline is followed, whereby 65% of these funds are planned for growth related capital projects, 25% for discretionary capital projects and 10% for future land development acquisitions.
Saskatoon land in conjunction with the CFO and the Finance Division monitor the cash position of this fund and as funds accumulate and become available for distribution, a dividend is declared.
In most cases, these dividends are allocated as possible funding for projects or to funding plans for major capital programs based on the distribution guidelines.

The discretionary allotment of these dividends can be put to any project, there has been a long standing practice of applying a portion of these funds generated from greenfield development to assist with infill and other housing developments such as the affordable housing reserve.

City accounts will approve through administrative reports and declarations of surplus funds from the neighborhood land development fund, as well as the use of these funds through the capital project budgets and the annual funding plan reports.
To date, $134.1 million from the fund have been declared and applied to many projects and reserves that have provided benefit to the citizens of Saskatoon as listed on the first page of the report.

And there are a number of future allocations expected from the fund in the near future totaling about $25 million of which the largest is a $10 million allocation as part of the funding plan for the north commuter parkway bridge and project and that's our report to worship.
